INTRODUCTION
           I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry, having been authorised
by the Committee, hereby present this One Hundred Seventieth Report on Demands for Grants (2004-05) pertaining to
the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries.
2.      The Committee in its meeting held on 30 th March, 2005 heard the Secretary, Ministry of ARI and the
representative of the attached organisations/offices of the Ministry on the issue of Demands for Grants (2005-06). A
detailed questionnaire was forwarded to the Ministry of ARI which were accordingly replied. The report has been
prepared on the basis of the replies received from the Ministry and the oral evidence of the Ministry of ARI on the
various aspect of the budgetary provisions.
3.      The Committee at its meeting held on 3rd May, 2005 considered and adopted the Report.

REPORT
1.1    The Agro and Rural Industries Sector is an important avenue for creation of employment in the rural non-farm
sector for the balanced economic growth of the country. The ARI sector seeks to establish village industries at low cost
based on the local raw materials, skills and technology for providing employment opportunities to the local population
and artisans who have been traditionally engaged in village level economic activities.
1.2    The Ministry acts as a nodal agency for promotion and development of agro and rural industries in small towns
and rural areas. The Charter for the Ministry is as follows:-
            1.Coordination of the development of village and cottage industries, and tiny/micro
enterprises in both urban and rural areas.
            2.Coordination of matters relating to all rural industries.
            3.Coir Industries. 
            4.The Coir Board.
            5.Prime Minister’s Rozgar Yojana (PMRY).
            6.Khadi and Village Industries Commission.
1.3    The Ministry guides and coordinates with the implementing agencies to ensure development and achievement as
per the set mandate. The Ministry has a multi-pronged role to play in the quality implementation of policies,
programmes and schemes. In the role of a policy maker, the Ministry collects, collates and derives inferences, which act
as critical inputs to further policy formulation/amendments. In the role of an advocate, the Ministry advocates and puts
up ‘felt needs’ of the stakeholders involved in the sector as a whole. In the role of a facilitator, the Ministry facilitates,
coordinates and supports its field agencies in implementing the programmes and schemes both quantitatively and
qualitatively.
1.4    The Committee understands that the creation of an independent Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries has
reinforced and strengthened the functioning of the ARI sector as a whole, by highlighting its present status and ensuring

5.0         MONITORING  MECHANISM
5.1    The main contribution of ARI sector to the national economy has been in terms of production and employment
generation through setting up of village industries in the rural and semi-urban areas. In the year 1955-56, the production
in terms of value under village industries was at the level of Rs. 10.93 crore, the same has gone up to Rs. 9228.27 crore
in 2003-04 and Rs. 8075 crore in 2004-05 (upto January, 2005). Similarly, employment level in Village Industries sector
has also increased from 3.07 lakh persons in 1955-56 to 65.40 lakh persons as on January, 2005.
5.2    To generate additional employment opportunities in rural areas, the Government launched the “Rural Employment
Generation Programme (REGP)”. In the Tenth five year plan, a target of 2 million jobs under REGP was fixed. This
target was enhanced to 2.5 million jobs in 2003-04. Accordingly, the employment targets were revised and fixed for
2003-04, 2004-05 and 2005-06 are 5 lakh, 5.25 lakh and 5.51 lakh respectively. During Tenth Plan period (upto
January, 2005), 10.89 lakh job opportunities have already been generated.
5.3    The Prime Minister’s Rozgar Yojana (PMRY) is another major scheme implemented by this Ministry. The scheme
seeks to create employment opportunities for 1.65 million persons over the Tenth Plan period. In the first two years of
Tenth Plan period, 5.93 lakh employment has been created under this Yojana. In 2004-05, the employment target has
been enhanced from 3.30 lakh persons to 3.75 lakh persons under this Yojana and 1.24 lakh employment have been
created (upto January, 2005).
5.4    The Coir industry provides employment to 5.86 lakh people mostly in rural sector. The contribution of this
industry to the GDP was estimated roughly at Rs.1750 crore during 2003-04. Out of this, the export earnings of the
industry was to the tune of Rs.407.50 crore. During 2004-05, the GDP is expected to be Rs. 1900 crore and the
contribution of this industry to the National Exchequer in foreign exchange is expected to be Rs.450 crore.
5.5    The monitoring mechanism at the Ministry level includes both structured as well as informal but regular
monitoring. Secretary (ARI) periodically monitors implementation of PMRY and REGP along with other scheme being
implemented by the Ministry. Secretary(ARI) also monitors the implementation of the National Common Minimum
Programme.
5.6    The fortnightly performances are reviewed at the level Secretary in the Ministry whereas KVIC and Coir Board
review monthly performances. As per the Management Information System approved by the Cabinet Secretariat for
Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries, implementation of PMRY, coir exports, and employment generation under
REGP and the declaration made in National Common Minimum Programme (NCMP) are reviewed. The activities of
KVIC, PMRY and Coir Schemes are also reviewed by Secretary on a monthly basis and a Brief Note is sent to the PMO
and Cabinet Secretary. On the basis of monthly and quarterly performances of progress in various sectors of
development, appropriate instructions are issued to KVIC, Coir Board and State Governments.
5.7    The performance of implementation of the schemes of KVIC and of Coir Board and the PMRY are reviewed at the
level of Head of the organisations and the States Governments. Progress of PMRY is also reviewed in the “Monitoring
Cell” constituted at RPCD, RBI Mumbai under the Chairmanship of Dy. Governor, RBI. The States and the banks have
been requested to monitor the target on monthly basis. Further, progress of the schemes is also reviewed on fortnightly
basis and precautionary measures to achieve the targets set is taken as warranted. In addition, performance of all
schemes have been analyzed at the time of formulation of budgetary proposals for the Ministry at RE stage.
5.8    The Committee is of the view that ARI sector can contribute to the national economy in terms of production and
employment generation through setting up of village industries in the rural and semi-urban areas. The efficacy and
effectiveness of the schemes largely depends upon intensive review of implementation of the schemes of KVIC, Coir
Board and the PMRY.

5.11  Poverty alleviation and employment generation are the keystone of the economic policy framework of the
Government. Thus, the economic philosophy behind the budget proposals 2005-06 is to empower the people, especially
the poor. In line with the above economic philosophy, the Budget proposal for the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries
for the year 2005-06 has received further support for creation of more employment on a sustainable basis in the rural
areas and small towns. Thus, the Budget allocation for generating more employment opportunities under REGP has
been increased from 326 crore in year 2004-05 (at RE stage) to Rs. 412 crore in 2005-06. However, for self-
employment generation under PMRY budget allocation has been kept at Rs. 218.50 crore in 2005-06 as was for 2004-
05.
5.12  In continuation of the economic philosophy for the budget 2005-06, welfare of the Khadi artisans have also been
taken care of by way of enhancing allocation under Khadi grant head from Rs. 90 crore (at RE stage) in 2004-05 to Rs.
110 crore in 2005-06 to meet the expenditure to cover insurance under the Group Insurance scheme of the KVIC.
Further, for regeneration of traditional industries such as coir, handloom, power loom, garment, rubber, cashew,
handicraft food processing, sericulture, wool development, leather, pottery and other cottage industries a scheme, titled
the Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI) has been drafted and the EFC note along with
the draft scheme has been circulated to the Ministries/Departments concerned for their comments on 15 th February,
2005.        The implementation of the scheme is expected to start in 2005-06, after necessary approval of the
EFC/Cabinet. Ministry of ARI has further informed that this will immensely help the rural artisans who have been
involved in their vocation for ages, but for want of adequate financial support were not able to upgrade the existing
technology. This in turn will help in more production in the traditional sector, thus leading to higher income generation
and better prosperity to the rural artisans.
5.13  The Committee expresses its concern over the provision of inadequate budgetary support to Ministry of ARI as the
projected demand was to the tune of Rs. 1150.10 crore against which Rs. 859.00 crore has been provide which may
affect the progress of the programmes undertaken by the Ministry. The Committee is of the considered view that since
ARI has potential for generating more employment opportunities in the rural areas and small towns, the Ministry of ARI
must vigorously and effectively take up the issue with the Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance urging for
additional allocation as per requirement at RE Stage.

8.1    The Prime Minister’s Rozgar Yojana (PMRY) scheme was launched on 2nd October, 1993 in the country. The
objective of the scheme is to assist educated unemployed youth from the weaker section of the society in setting up
micro enterprises in all economically viable activities as per the parameters of the scheme .The scheme is implemented
in both urban & rural areas of the country from 1994-95 onwards. The objective of the Prime Minister’s Rozgar Yojana
(PMRY) is to mitigate the problem of unemployment amongst the educated unemployed youth in urban and rural areas
through setting up of self employed tiny units. The scheme is a central sector scheme. The Central Government provides
funds for subsidy, training, supervision and other software support. The District Industry Centers and the Directorate of
Industries are mainly responsible for Implementation of the scheme along with the banks.
8.2    The scheme is being monitored centrally by the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries. The States and the banks
are the implementing agencies at the field level. The beneficiaries under the scheme are identified by the field level
agencies and the loan component for setting up the micro enterprises is provided by the banks to the beneficiaries. The
unemployed youth are expected to apply to the DICs. A task force at the DIC level conducts the preliminary screening
and suitable applications are then forwarded to the banks who undertake a detailed scrutiny and thereafter sanction the
loan. A managerial training is given to the beneficiaries whose cases have been sanctioned, before the actual disbursal
of the loan.

9.2   Keeping in view the inflation and general increase in the income level and also the fact that some States like West
Bengal, Gujarat, Pondicherry etc. are running their own self employment schemes with better subsidy provision as
compared to PMRY, the Committee recommends the following modification in the existing criteria of PMRY scheme:
           (i)Enhancement of the eligibility criteria of family income from Rs. 40,000/- per annum to Rs. 1,50,000/- per
annum.
           (ii)Enhancement in project cost ceiling under the scheme may be enhanced from 
Rs. 1,00,000/- to Rs. 2,00,000/- for business sector and from Rs. 2,00,000/- to 
Rs. 5,00,000/- for service and industry sector.
           (iii)Enhancement in subsidy from Rs. 7,500/- per beneficiary (except for NER, J&K, Himachal Pradesh and
Uttaranchal) to Rs. 20,000/- per beneficiary other than NE States, J&K, Himachal Pradesh and Uttaranchal.
In case of NE States including Sikkim, J&K, Himachal Pradesh and Uttaranchal, the subsidy ceiling may be
enhanced i.e. Rs. 25,000/- per beneficiary.

17.0         PROBLEMS BEING FACED BY KHADI INDUSTRIES
            (i)Quality:- In the market economy, is an important aspect. As such, to make khadi products competitive in the
market it is necessary to enhance the quality of the products as such to enhance the budget support for such
schemes.
            (ii)Sales outlets:- Shabby & dilapidated conditions of khadi institutions is a weak area which require
improvement for attracting the customers. A scheme has been launched for this purpose by formulating a
plan for modernization and renovation of sales outlets. KVIC has already renovated and modernized one of
the prestigious DSOs located at Connaught Place, New Delhi and another private sales outlet at Khan
Market, New Delhi. Further under UNDP-KVIC project, computerization of inventory management and
financial accounting is one of the important element and in this regard, 10 major sales outlets were
identified and upgraded. The proposal for renovation of other DSOs and Institutional Sales Outlets need
adequate budgetary support. Similarly, the efforts initiated by KVIC by launching the PRODIP for
improving the Product Design and Packaging also taken up for vigorous follow up with adequate financial
support.
            (iii)    Working capital:- Shortage of working capital is another major problem blocking the progress of khadi
programme. Earlier, the institutions were enjoying working capital assistance from KVIC’s budgetary
support at zero rate of interest. Subsequently, in view of budgetary crunch, the khadi institutions have been
directed to avail of funds from banking sector, against which KVIC issues interest subsidy eligibility
certificate. However, the financial institutions are not honouring the ISEC issued by KVIC to its full extent
as such there is shortage of working capital in the Khadi Sector. Further, large amount of pending rebate
with various State Governments adds to the burden.
            (iv)Consortium Bank Credit (CBC):- As on 31 st January, 2005, Rs. 238.02 crore was lying as outstanding
balance with Khadi Implementing Agencies under Consortium Bank Credit (CBC) for which they have to
pay interest @ 4.5 per cent in addition to refunding the same in instalments whereas under the working
fund system adopted for khadi programme the institutions are permitted to keep the working capital in the
form of working fund as long as they maintain certain level of production. The Government has now
approved the conversion of outstanding balance under CBC scheme into working capital and for this
purpose KVIC has executed necessary documents and forwarded to the lead bank - State Bank of India.
            (v)Outdated and obsolete charkhas and looms:- Another area which required immediate assistance to khadi
institutions is tools and implements. The fact remains that the charkhas and looms available with them are
mostly outdated, which require replacement or renovation.

budgetory support with the Ministry of Finance and the Planning Commission for modernisation and renovation of sales
outlets, alongwith the strategy and time frame to execute the same. Adequate steps must also be taken for modernisation

20.8  The Committee notes the submission of the Ministry of ARI that KVIC is adopting a strategy to generate large
scale employment in rural sector by channelising institutional finance. A Working Group constituted by Planning
Commission for the Tenth Five Year Plan has recommended employment target of 89.57 lakh (15 lakh under Khadi and

allocated Rs. 2080 crore to KVIC. Under its REGP scheme, it is proposed to generate 25 lakh employment by the
terminal year of Tenth Five Year Plan. The Committee is of the considered view that an all out efforts should be made
for achieving the target set by the Planning Commission. The Committee wishes to point out that while combating the
problem of unemployment and especially setting the target (that should be determined/ fixed time frame) proper and
adequate attention must be paid to population growth rate and the prevalence of level of poverty so that the problem of
unemployment, poverty and population explosion may be solved in a time bound frame with a holistic approach.
20.9  The Committee understands that the Government Department/Ministries functions with specific mandate,
however, there is the need for comprehensive and coordinated emphasis for tackling the intrinsic problems of the
national economy. The Committee desires the problem of national economy should be tackled through comprehensive
and intergraded planning and having coordination and collaboration among Governments Departments/Ministries for
effective outcome/result within a stipulated time frame. Of course, the role of private enterprising units would also be
significant in achieving such national goal, therefore, their participation should also be encouraged.
21.0         MARKETING STRATEGY FOR KVI
21.1  The marketing strategy of KVIC is to focus on its eco friendly and natural product range. Khadi and Village
Industries sector produces goods and services both. In village industries service based units basically cover local area
needs. With regard to non-consumer goods normally units established have good market as most of such products are
intermediary products used by other industries. Main difficulty is in consumer goods and khadi. For both these products
areas of intervention involves a detailed marketing strategy for publicity, branding and brand promotion, design input,
better packaging etc. Accessing private marketing channel, modernization of existing channels, organizing large scale
exhibitions are important aspects. Design/packaging development scheme and renovation of marketing outlets scheme
has been launched.
21.2  For the consumer goods, KVIC has developed “Sarvodaya Brand” consisting of FMCG products like Toilet Soap,
Pickles, Honey, etc., “Khadi” for exclusive up-market and export products like Essential Oils, Herbal Products,
Designer Garments etc. and “Desi Aahaar” for Organic foods like Cereals, Spices Powder, Pulses, etc. and the same
have been launched at Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata etc. in select Outlets. Based on the experience it is felt that a
professional Marketing Agency / Federation is required, so that KVIC does not get involved in Departmental Trading
Activities, since institutions and marketing professionals can play a better and effective role in marketing these
products. Accordingly a Marketing Confederation has been constituted out of existing Khadi & VI Federations and has
also been accorded provisional recognition by KVIC. The Confederation is expected to take up aggressive marketing for
KVI products with active support of KVIC.
22.0         MARKETING OF PRODUCTS UNDER KVIC
22.1  There are 7050 Sales Outlets under KVI Sector and in addition, KVIC has launched a scheme of Franchise Outlets
as well as marketing into private channel of distribution. A scheme for opening Sales Outlets under REGP Scheme has
also been introduced. There is a need for supporting inputs like CFCs in a big way for providing infrastructural support
to marketing like raw-material godown, processing facilities, quality control laboratories, packaging, etc.
22.2  In addition, exhibitions are conducted every year for sale as well as promotion of KVI goods. The institutions
working under KVI sector also conduct Mobile Sales as well as door-to-door sales for sale of their goods. Most of the
goods produced in VI as well as REGP units go through the marketing through private trade channel. There is an
eminent need to strengthen the distribution channel of VI goods by setting up Gramodyog agar on the lines of Khadi
Vastragar.
22.3         Government Supply also forms a major part in marketing the KVI products. Under DGS&D, Rate Contract,
KVIC used to supply Khadi as well as other village industries product to different organizations, prominent among them
being the Indian Railway, Defence, Paramilitary Forces and other Government Departments.

in May, 1977 which provides Interest Subsidy to the extent of the difference between the actual interest charged by the
banks and 4 per cent born by the institutions. In view of the recommendations made by the High Power Committee
(HPC) in 1994, the ISEC scheme is now extended only to Khadi and Ployvastra Programme with effect from 1995-96.
However, under Village Industries activities fund already committed earlier ISEC are also provided, which constituted
only in a small quantum. As the Khadi institutions were to pay zero per cent interest on this loan till 2003 and 4 per cent
thereafter, KVIC have hardly been able to pay any interest or return the loan advanced by Government to KVIC. The
amount of interest accrued to KVIC on loan has been subsidized by the Government through payment of subsidy in lieu
of interest over the years.
36.2  The Committee was informed by the Ministry of ARI that the subsidy in lieu of interest is not actually released to
the KVIC but is provided for in the budgetary provision both Plan and Non-plan for book adjustments, against the
interest payable by KVIC to Government. The Committee endorses the provision made for the purpose. The budgetary
provision for interest subsidy as a book adjustment is arising on account of the fact that the sanction of Khadi and VI
loan at different points of time over the years has borne varying rates of interest, (varying between 11.8 per cent to 14
per cent) whereas KVIC being a developmental agency for promoting rural employment through Khadi and VI activities
has in turn lent to its beneficiaries at zero per cent interest till 16 March, 2000 and at 4 per cent afterwards (Khadi Loan)
and VI loan at the rate of 4 per cent per annum. The subsidy is therefore towards this difference in the rate at which
KVIC borrows from the Government and the rate at which it lends to beneficiaries. The Committee finds it reasonable
that since the amount of interest subsidy has been accumulating every year, the budgetary provision for interest subsidy
has been kept at the level of Rs. 39.10 crore to meet the requirements of annual book adjustment.

in KVI activities.
38.4  The main implementing agencies of village industries are individual entrepreneurs, however, the subsidy in lieu of
interest was meant only for VI institutions and entrepreneurs were not covered. By launching Margin Money scheme

channelising the institutional credit with corresponding of Margin Money from KVIC. Initially the Margin Money

42.4  The performance under the NPRI Scheme has not been satisfactory at all. Some of the reasons to this could be the

of Finance (MoF). The EFC note along with the revised draft scheme has been circulated to the Ministries/Departments
concerned for their comments on 15 February, 2005.
42.6  The Committee takes stock of the fact that NPRI which was announced in the budget 
1999-2000 with the objective of setting up of hundred rural industrial clusters in the country every year for boosting
rural economy by creating more employment avenues and to arrest the migration of the rural artisans or town/cities. The
irony of the programme was that no separate fund was made available to implement the programme and it was
conceived that since the various Ministries/Departments are having their own programme in this “coveted areas and
their co-ordination and synergistic harnessing would be significant/harness the objectives of the programmes. The result
that comes out is that the expectation regarding the success of the programme felled apart, and that was bound to happen
with the programme without financial support.
42.7  The Committee observes that the co-ordination and synergetic approach so conceived among various Government
Ministries/Departments to make NPRI a success could not succeed the test of the time and the administrative (Ministry
of ARI) which was supposed to implement the NPRI spent no time in screwing the bureaucratic skill for advocating the
countless reasons for “unsatisfactory performance of NPRI i.e. meagre financial assistance of Rs. 5.00 lakh for lakh per
cluster for wide intervention, fill in gap arrangements, non-availability of credit linked subsidy component and also the
inadequate synergy with the Ministries / Departments with their own scheme in this area. When this Committtee
recommended for comprehensive over hauling and synchronization of all schemes and programmes for employment
generation and poverty alleviation, it the Ministry of ARI who beautifully referred the allocation of transaction of
business among various Government’s Ministries/Departments with a stress that sufficient co-ordination and syenergy
exists among various Government’s Ministries/Departments. The Committee wonders as how the same Ministry of ARI
is now wanting out the lack of co-ordination and synergy as the reason for unsatisfactory performance of NPRI. This
Committee is of the view that logic and argument of the Ministry of ARI is of selective nature.
42.8  Regarding NPRI, the Committee in its Report on Demands for Grants (2004-05) that NPRI has the potential for
actual rural industrialization and consolidation of rural economy and had recommended that the Government should
undertake concrete measures to combat the problems in achieving the objectives, targets credit-flow, implementation
and monitoring mechanism and “Key Concern Areas” of NPRI. But of no avail. Sensing the slow but sure death knell of
the NPRI, the Ministry of ARI has now decided to abandon the so acclaimed programme (NPRI) and the Ministry
comes out with re-christened programme, coincidently, the name of the programme is SFURTI, Scheme of Funds for
Re-genration of Traditional Industries. NPRI had made a slow start, therefore, it seems that the name of the new
programme is carefully drafted as SFURTI, obviously to instill the hope among those who is using their heart in the
efficient working of the Government machinery.
42.9  The Committee is awefully shocked to observe the pathetic working of the programmes/ schemes and the
monitoring mechanism as maintained within the Governmental structure which is being imparted to make the
programme a success. The Committee is of the considered view that re-christening of schemes is not the guarantee to
make the new scheme a success unless and until the scheme is back by adequate financial fund and willing
administrative backup to deliver in the system.The Committee has no objection with launching of new programme like
SFURTI or with whatever names it comes in future but the Committee strongly feels that NPRI has cherished national
goal and appropriate objectives and had no inherent weaknesses/problems as such except the lack of allocation for a
separate fund, the Committee therefore, reiterates that NPRI must continue in order to achieve those goals/objectives
and a separate fund must be allocated to NPRI.

49.0         STRATEGY TO PROMOTE INTER-SECTORAL CO-OPERATION AND ASSISTANCE
49.1  Regarding the suggestions for inter-sectoral cooperation and assistance among various sectors of economy to
promote Agro and Rural Industries. The Ministry of ARI stated that the Ministry of ARI, Rural Development and Food
Processing are quite different and do not overlap except in a few areas. The work of M/o Food Processing relates to the
promotion of industries like processing and refrigeration, technical assistance planning, development and control
of/assistance to the industries in the food sector viz. bread, oilseeds, beer, alcoholic drinks from molasses base, aerated
water etc. whereas, the work of M/o Rural Development relates to public cooperation including the matters relating to
Panchayati Raj/Panchayati Raj institutions rural development etc., rural employment, integrated rural development,
matters relating to rural connectivity including Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, rural housing etc. The work of the
Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries is to coordinate the development work of village andcottage industries and tiny
and micro enterprises in both urban and rural areas and the matter relating to all rural industries.
49.2  It was further stated that though the role of M/o Rural Development is poverty alleviation and that of M/o ARI is
employment generation, in case of Ministry of Rural Development, the projects taken up are meant for the people below
poverty line and per unit investment is around Rs. 50,000/-, whereas in Ministry ofARI, the emphasis is on employment
generation through individual entrepreneurs and the project cost can go upto Rs. 25 lakhs. Thus in case of M/o ARI, the
individual enterprises are encouraged for setting up projects for generating  employment opportunities. In case of
Ministry of Food Processing Industries, the focus is on the specialized area of food processing and covers all types of
projects including large scale projects.
49.3  The Ministry of ARI advocated that the holistic planning for overall development of rural economy is already
being done at the level of Planning Commission. The Planning Commission has broken down the national targets with
the targets at the Ministry level in consultation with the concerned Ministries/State Governments for the Tenth Plan
period. These targets are reviewed regularly. Further, the Planning Commission also sets up Inter-Ministerial Task
Force (1MTF) whenever it is felt necessary to integrate the efforts of more than one Ministry. During 2004-05, the
Ministry of ARI was in several such IMTFs viz. Household and Artisanal Manufacturing, Agriculture and allied
activities, etc.
49.4  The Committee understands that each Ministry has been interested with specific mandate and each of them
functions on the areas as per the mandate. The Committee also understands that Planning Commission coordinates the
programmes on various issues. However, governance can not be water compartmentalised all together in the cases were
the areas/issues/concerned are of similar nature or overlap each other as is the case with the ARI sector which has to
promote industries in the rural areas and thus generate avenues of employment generation with the ultimate objectives
of poverty alleviation and thus contributing the national economy. Therefore, the Committee is of view that strategy to
promote inter-sectoral co-operation and assistance among Rural Development, poverty alleviation programmes, Food
Processing sector and other such programmes/schemes with the Agro & Rural Sector in order to give greater thrust and
coordinated efforts and synergistic approach towards implementation of rural infrastructural development projects,
employment Generation and Rural industrialization & Development and poverty-alleviation. The Government should
adopt the Unified and Integrated and holistic approach to strike out the very roots of poverty and undertake the
implementation of well knitted policies/programmes to develop the rural economy with co-ordinated and concerted
efforts, then and only then benefits of the programmes would percolate down to the targets contributing to “Bharat
Nirman”.

51.0         IMPACT OF GLOBALISATION AND LIBERALIZATION
51.1  The impact of liberalization has enhanced the competitive nature of the whole industrial set up as such. Open
market mechanisms have come in place of regulated and protected nature of pre-liberalized economy. The challenge
posed by globalized economy has enhanced and enabled nurturing of the inherent competitive and resilient nature of the
Agro and Rural Industries sector as such.
51.2  The sector mainly consists of Khadi, Village Industries, cottage industries (handicrafts), Coir, Tiny and Micro
enterprises. The products of this sector by their very nature are traditional, location specific and exclusively indigenous.
This adds to the specialized and exclusive nature of the sector as such and gives it a dynamic and resilient character. For
example, herbal products, organic manure, organic food, honey production, traditional crafts items, etc are so exclusive
by nature that it offers immense export potential which is almost non-competitive in the world economy. This defines
the future outlook of the sector. The emphasis would be to highlight the exclusivity of ARI products and its suitability to
specific local area both for production as well as marketing as it addresses the felt local needs and to develop quality
diversification and aggressively enter the world market.

52.0  LEGAL FRAMEWORK SUPPORTING OF THE AGRO & RURAL INDUSTRIES
52.1  The existing legal framework pertains to specific Acts framed for the implementing agencies like the KVIC Act
and the legislations relating to Coir sector. Within the broad legislative frameworks of these Acts, the Khadi and Village
Industries Commission as well as the Coir Board frame their rules of business and conduct their activities. Some
modifications, as required, in the basic legal framework have also been made.
52.2  Further, in the National Common Minimum Programme, the Government has declared to revamp the KVIC.
Towards this objective, the Government has dissolved the KVIC with effect from 14 October, 2004 and also set up a
ten-Member Expert Committee to Examine the Structure, Functioning and Performance of KVIC and recommend
Measures to revamp the KVIC and launch new programmes, with the following terms of reference:
            (i)     to review the existing structure, functioning and performance of the KVIC since its inception;
            (ii)     to review the Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act, 1956 (No. 61 of 1956), KVIC Rules 1957,
and the Regulations made thereunder and to recommend restructuring, along with modifications, if any, in
these statutes, to achieve the objectives of (a) development of Khadi and Village Industries (KVI) and (b)
making KVIC a more professional and effective body for implementation of the existing KVI
programmes/schemes and/or launching new programmes/schemes with a view to enhancing employment
and income generation in the rural areas and expending the markets for (including export of) Khadi and
Village Industry products; and
            (iii)    to recommend any other measure(s) considered necessary by the Committee to revamp the KVIC and to
launch new, appropriate programmes/schemes.
52.3  The Expert Committee is expected to give its recommendation shortly. The Government will take necessary action
on the recommendations of the Expert Committee including changes in the legal framework as required to make KVIC
more effective in generation of employment opportunities in the rural areas and small towns.
52.4  The Committee hopes that the recommendations of the expert Committee on revamping KVIC would go a long
way in reorienting the organisational and functional pattern of KVIC for the promotion and proliferation of Khadi and
Village Industries.

53.1  Reacting to the suggestion of the need for formulation of the national policy of Agro and Rural Industries, the
Ministry of ARI the viewed that the present policy relating to Agro and Rural Industries adequately addresses the issues
and potentials of the sector. Khadi and Village Industries sector through its Khadi package tackles the issue of
liberalization and its after effects effectively. The policy framework at present is adequately ensures optimal support and
promotion to the units functioning in this sector. Policy initiatives in response to the changed economic scenario and its
challenges are being consistently addressed by the Ministry through a dynamic process of policy amendments and
positioning.
53.2  The Committee feels that the Ministry of ARI should give serious thought for formulation of National Policy for
Agro & Rural Industries for the growth of rural industries, instead of rejecting the suggestion on the first instance. Had
the every thing been right with the existing policy measures, India’s Agro Rural Industries would have been in a better
position contributing the national economy and particularly consolidating the rural economy. The Committee
understands that the Ministry through a dynamic process of policy amendments and positioning is consistently
addressing policy initiatives in response to the changed economic scenario and its challenges, however, the colossal
problem of India is also persisting and that too consistently. Therefore, it is desirable that the Ministry of ARI should act
and not react on the recommendation of the Committee without giving a proper thought to the ideas behind the
recommendations.
54.0         PROBLEMS BEING FACED BY AGRO & RURAL INDUSTRIES
54.1  The Major problems faced by the Agro and Rural Industries, are primarily relating to lack of Infrastructural
facilities, marketing linkages and updated technology. The same is being addressed by way of providing emphasis on
development of market linkages, modernization of outlets, diversification of products, exposure to foreign markets and
infrastructural back up through cluster development. The impact of liberalization and WTO regime on the market
scenario are being responded by the Sector through policy initiatives which enhances the resilient nature of the sector as
a whole.
54.2  The Committee is of the view that Ministry of ARI should interact with the concerned sector/department
for facilitating infrastructural facilities, marketing linkages and updated technology to the Agro and Rural
Industries.

55.0  CREDIT FLOW TO AGRO & RURAL INDUSTRIES
55.1  Major credit flow to the Agro and Rural Industries is through banks. Credit flow to units in this sector is supported
by way of Margin Money/subsidy/loan/working capital. The loan part is accessed through the financial institutions and
the subsidy and margin money part of the project is borne form the budgetary allocations to the concerned implementing
agency. Problems by way of unviable projects, cutting down financial size of the projects, lengthy procedural
formalitiesare faced in general by the beneficiaries or entrepreneurs in accessing credit for their units. This may be, to a
certain extent linked to unsatisfactory recovery of finances advanced. Hence the attempt is to constantly, vigorously
pursue recovery dues and at the same time ensure easy accessibility to new entrepreneurs.
55.2  The Committee feels that the fiscal measures/issues may be undertaken by the Ministry of ARI with the Ministry
of Finance to boost investment in Agro and Rural Industries through credit enabled private investment and enhanced
public investment effective measures for Agro & Rural Industries for striking an equilibrium for balanced regional
growth and overall national economic growth and development.
55.3  The rural industries provide the critical forum needed for a balanced regional growth due to its unique resilient and
vibrant qualities as a sector which spans the Nation as a whole. With the sector being a combination of traditional skills
coupled with modern technology provides a very strong and potential weapon to combat the negative effects of
liberalization. It is an accepted fact that in our country, with regional imbalances as they exist, liberalization without the
presence of this sector would have made the existing imbalances extreme and a potent threat to the objectives of rural
industrialization and poverty alleviation. It is in this scenario that this independent Ministry, focusing totally on this
sector, formulating policies to withstand the effects of liberalization, assumes its critical role in shaping the national
economic scenario. The measures taken so far by the Ministry should effectively enable the achievement of balanced
regional growth.
55.4  The Committee acknowledges the contribution of ARI sector and awareness of the  responsibilities of Ministry of
ARI for a balanced regional growth, however, the Committee expects that the Ministry of ARI would undertake
effective measures for Agro and Rural Industries for striking an equilibrium for balanced regional growth and overall
national economic growth and development.
56.0         EMPLOYMENT GENERATION IN AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES
56.1  Under the Khadi and Village industries sector so far approximately 74.01 lakh persons have been provided
employment. Similarly under PMRY employment up to January, 2005 has been generated to the tune of 31.6 lakh
persons. In the Coir sector about 5.8 lakh coir workers are being gainfully employed. The disguised employment in this
sector is primarily of the Khadi artisans whereas in other avenues it is not so pronounced. However, the Government has
not undertaken any survey so far in this regard.
56.2  The Committee is of the considered view that there is the tremendous potential for employment generation in the
Agro and Rural Industries, need is to frame the policy measures and chalking out suitable strategy to harness the
inherent potential of employment generation in the ARI sector. In this regard, the Committee desires the Government
would come out with integrated and holistic programme for employment generation and poverty alleviation. Investment
- employment generation - enhancement in purchasing power - improvement in standard of living and the consequent
poverty alleviation route would root out the inherent problems India’s economy. The Committee hopes that the Ministry
of ARI would understand its responsibility towards changing the status of the country from the developing to a
developed one and act upon with all efforts.

58.0         INSTITUTIONALIZATION OF AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES
58.1  At the level of Centre-State as well as the Districts there is both structural as well as informal coordination and
exchange of ideas and information. The District level implementing agency for most of the programmes and schemes
devolve at the level of the District Collectors and his offices. Hence, at the District level there is one agency, which
ensures coordination both effectively and efficiently. State-level, again, agencies for coordination are also specified and
interaction relating to policy as well as implementation is ensured. At the apex level also there is frequent and both
formal and informal interaction with the related Ministries to achieve better coordination and collaboration amongst
agencies involved in similar activities. The Ministry of ARI, along with management of its activities, functions on the
basis of its avowed objective/mission, which is to promote and strengthen the Agro and Rural Industries sector.
58.2  The Committee is of the considered opinion the Ministry of ARI must undertake measures for better co-ordination
and collaboration among various agencies/ operating at centre, state and district level so that agro and rural industries
may be given a look of organized sector where all activities can be carried out/managed by stated objectives and
cherished Mission. In this regard, the Ministry of ARI should be guided by Management by Objectives (MBO )and not
merely management by activities.
59.0  “NEW DEAL” FOR RURAL INDIA
59.1  The Prime Minister in his address to the Nation has laid stress on overall growth of the national economy.
Employment generation has been identified as a tool to banish poverty, hunger and homelessness and improve the
standard of living of the mass of our people. The employment should be generated through environmentally sustainable
rural industries. The Prime Minister has also focused on expanding opportunities for gainful employment in agriculture
and in non-farm rural activities.
59.2  Since the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries is functioning in the rural sector, the interaction between farmner
and agro industries has greatly picked up. To improve interaction between farmers and agro industries, KVIC has taken
several measures to strengthen activities in the rural areas like bee-keeping, food processing industries, handmade paper
industries etc. These programmes along with other activities of the Ministry in the agro and rural sector will continue to
receive focus in the Ministry in line with the message enshrined in PMs speech with a view to empower disadvantaged
sections of the society.

60.0  RURAL INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT FUND (RIDF)
60.1  The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) being operated by NABARD under Ministry of Rural
Development is for the purpose of financing projects like irrigation, flood protection, watershed management,
construction of rural roads and bridges etc. in the rural areas, whereas the Ministry of ARI is concerned with providing
employment in the non-farm sector through setting up of agro and rural industries. As such, the RIDF is not directly
concerned with this Ministry. However, because of better connectivity to be created in the rural areas by way of roads
and bridges under RIDF, the setting up agro and rural industries would definitely be helped in so far as quicker
availability of raw materials and marketing of the products are concerned. This will have spiraling effect on further
growth of agro and rural industries.

(RIDF) with a corpus of Rs. 8000.00 crore would go a long way in the proliferation and setting up of new units of agro

AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION
         The Committee refers to the concern expressed by the Finance Minister in the General Budget 2005-06 and the
need to tackle the twin problem of unemployment and poverty with focused and co-ordinated approach. The Committee
appreciates the approach of the Finance Minister as stated in the General Budget 2005-06 which is in consonance with
the recommendation of the Committee given in its Report on Demands for Grants (2004-05). The Committee’s
observation in that report reads as under:-
“The Committee is pleased to note that the Government is extending adequate attention to the rural sector and
especially the Agro and Rural Industries. The Committee, however, desires that the Government should come
out with pragmatic planning for Agro and Rural Industries keeping in view the twin objectives of employment
generation and poverty alleviation. The Committee wishes to highlight that the Agro and Rural Industries has
the potential of employment generation and since large chunk of Indian population dwells in rural areas under
the abject poverty therefore, holistic and comprehensive planning for rural sector and its effective
implementation is the need of the hour.”
(Para 31.4 of Report No. 152nd)
         The Committee in its 124th Report on Demands for Grants 2003-04 had recommended as under:-
“The Committee is of the opinion that Government should fix the target under PMRY keeping in mind the stark
reality of population growth rate, quantum of poverty and absolute number of unemployment (disguised
unemployment as well as seasonal employment). Need of the hour is formulation of Integrated and Total
Planning after having objective assessment of empirical fact and figures. The rate of employment generations
must be twice/thrice than the population growth rate so that the problem of unemployment gets out rooted in a
time bound manner. The Committee would be pleased to observe that the planning is done for exploring
employment generation at the geo­metrical rate and population growth be limited at the arithmetical rate.
Though at the first instance the suggestion may seem illusive but to change the fate of India it has to be done
and Government must strive in this direction. This is possible only through co-ordinated and total Planning and
when the problems of Population, Poverty and unemployment are studied and visualized in a holistic manner
and policy-maker has to go beyond the cocoon of department/ministries of the Government.”
(Para 7.6.3 of 124th Report)
         What the Finance Minister is pronouncing in the General Budget (2005-06), the Committee has been observing
and making recommendations since its report on Demands for Grants 
(2003-04). The Committee therefore, expects that the two wings of the Government should not act in water tight
compartmentalization manner. The problem of unemployment and poverty are intrinsically related to each other
therefore, focused and co-ordinated approach is required, then and only then India’s Developing Economy can be
converted into a developed one at a rapid track and within stipulated time-frame.     (Paras 57.2, 57.3 and 57.4)

“NEW DEAL” FOR RURAL INDIA
         The Committee understands that the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries is functioning in the rural sector and
thus ARI sector can be a party to the “New Deal” for rural India in respect to rural development and welfare and for
achieving sustained overall annual growth of generating employment. The “New Deal” for rural India would benefit to
the agro and rural industries lead to empowerment of disadvantaged sections of the society. The Committee is of the
opinion that suitable steps should be taken to boost the growth of agro based industries and diversification and
development of agro processed products for enhancing it contribution in Bharat Nirman.         (Para 59.4)
RURAL INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT FUND (RIDF)
         The Committee understands that the announcement of re-launching Rural Infrastructure Development Fund
(RIDF) with a corpus of Rs. 8000.00 crore would go a long way in the proliferation and setting up of new units of agro
rural industries in the country. Even if the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) is operated by NABARD
under Ministry of Rural Development, the basic infrastructure and better connectivity is to be created in the rural areas
by way of roads and bridges under RIDF, which would lead to promotion and proliferation of ARI in the country. The
Ministry of ARI may co-ordinate with the Ministry of Rural Development for apportioning the fund also in the better
interest of ARI.         (Para 60.2)
